sources.title: Gavin Newsom: birth, education, PlumpJack business and political chronology
sources.findings: Read the California State Library biography and its speech-date list. It confirms Gavin Christopher Newsom’s birth on 10 October 1967 in San Francisco, 1989 political-science graduation from Santa Clara, a partial baseball scholarship, a 1992 retail wine shop, 1997 appointment to the Board of Supervisors, and subsequent statewide election history. The original business was a San Francisco retail shop, not a winery first established in Oakville. Educational sources differ on BA versus BS, so retain the verified political-science degree without a degree-type abbreviation. Election in 2003 is not the 2004 mayoral oath, and election in 2018 is not the 2019 gubernatorial oath. The speech index supplies dates, not a read of every speech.

sources.title: Gavin Newsom: Democratic governor, prior offices and inauguration dates
sources.findings: Read the National Governors Association’s current-governor profile. It confirms Democratic Party affiliation, date of birth, prior mayoral and lieutenant-governor roles, and lists inauguration dates of 7 January 2019 and 6 January 2023. The second entry is used for the inauguration ceremony, not an independently determined constitutional term-start calculation. Praise of his leadership and policy agenda is advocacy-style profile language, not an independent evaluation of success. Family details were not necessary to the public dossier.

sources.title: 4 May 2026 profile: local career, elections, pandemic controversy and state leadership
sources.findings: Read CNN Editorial Research’s 4 May 2026 chronology syndicated on KTVZ. It supports the 1996 commission appointment, 1997 supervisor appointment, 1998 election, 2003 mayoral election and 2007 re-election, 2004 marriage-licence episode and subsequent invalidation, 2010/2014 lieutenant-governor elections, 2018/2022 gubernatorial elections, and pandemic-era restaurant attendance and apology. Its BS label is not chosen over conflicting BA descriptions elsewhere; use the degree and year established by the state library. The 2004 ruling on municipal authority did not itself determine all subsequent constitutional marriage questions. The 2020 conduct is recorded as a documented political controversy and apology, not a criminal finding. Private relationship history and medical details were not necessary and were omitted.

sources.title: 8 January 2004: actual oath as San Francisco’s 42nd mayor
sources.findings: Read Rachel Gordon’s contemporaneous 8 January 2004 mayoral-inauguration account. Newsom took the oath that day as the 42nd mayor, succeeding Willie Brown after the December runoff. His housing and homelessness priorities were stated goals, not completed outcomes. Youngest in a century is not youngest mayor ever; no superlative is carried into the profile. The story’s comments about future bonds and staffing are not treated as implemented measures, and older family references are not current marital-status evidence.

sources.title: January 2011 successor-mayor motion confirms Newsom’s lieutenant-governor oath on 10 January
sources.findings: Read the Board of Supervisors motion appointing Edwin Lee and its adoption record. It explicitly records Newsom’s completed lieutenant-governor oath at 1:25 p.m. on 10 January 2011, creating the mayoral vacancy. The motion was passed on 11 January, while a draft footer says 4 January and an earlier nomination meeting was 7 January; none replaces the 10 January oath date. The vacancy confirmation overrides shorthand biographies ending his mayoralty in 2010. The source does not establish that Lee’s later full term began at the time Newsom was sworn in.

sources.title: Certified summary of the 14 September 2021 gubernatorial recall vote
sources.findings: Read the secretary of state’s final one-page recall summary. It records 7,944,092 no votes (61.9%) and 4,894,473 yes votes (38.1%) on the recall question and explicitly says Newsom remained in office. Percentages for the replacement-candidate question have a different denominator and cannot be treated as a direct two-person contest against him. Surviving recall continued his existing term; it was not a new four-year election. The underlying statewide certification materials were not comprehensively audited beyond this official summary.

sources.title: 6 January 2023: second-term inauguration and prepared address
sources.findings: Read the 6 January 2023 inauguration notice and relevant portions of the prepared address. The release reports a completed second-term inauguration; the remarks are labelled prepared, so not every written line is certified as delivered. The 8 November 2022 election is separately corroborated by CNN. The ceremony’s anniversary and political criticism of opponents are not independent findings about every policy dispute. Do not turn this ceremonial date into a separate calculation of the legal commencement of the constitutional term.

sources.title: 29 September 2025: SB 53 signing and frontier-AI transparency, reporting and whistleblower provisions
sources.findings: Read the 29 September 2025 SB 53 signing release, including its What the law does section. It identifies Senator Scott Wiener as author, Newsom as signer, large-frontier-developer framework disclosure, critical-safety-incident reporting and whistleblower protection. This is state legislation, not a federal statute, and publication of a framework does not certify any model as safe. CalCompute is a consortium and planning framework, not proof that a public compute cluster was already operational. Promotional claims about being the birthplace of AI or first in the nation and company valuation statistics are not adopted. The final statute, agency implementation and later litigation were not separately reviewed.

sources.title: 16 September 2022: climate-law package and AB 1279 carbon-neutrality target
sources.findings: Read the 16 September 2022 climate-signing announcement and the AB 1279 section. It codifies a goal of statewide carbon neutrality no later than 2045. Projected jobs, economic savings, pollution reductions and future clean-energy targets are forecasts or policy commitments, not achieved results. The governor acted with the legislature; the programme is not his sole personal invention. No claim about the present legal status of the separate 2035 vehicle regulation or every oil-setback provision is inferred from this historical release.

sources.title: 16 September 2021: housing package, SB 9 and housing-supply objectives
sources.findings: Read the 16 September 2021 housing-package announcement, including SB 9’s duplex/lot-split purpose. SB 8, SB 9 and SB 10 are distinct bills; SB 10’s voluntary city zoning process is not silently attributed to SB 9. Funding and estimated unit counts are plans, not an independently measured number of completed homes. Approval reform is not proof that homelessness ended or housing affordability was restored. Detailed current eligibility is bounded by the housing department’s fact sheet rather than treating all parcels as eligible.

sources.publisher: California Department of Housing and Community Development
sources.title: September 2024 SB 9 fact sheet: eligible lots, housing units and ministerial approval
sources.findings: Read the September 2024 HCD fact sheet’s executive summary, single-family-zone scope and ministerial-review definition. It confirms environmental, tenant and historic-property conditions and describes approval without discretionary review for eligible projects. Up to four units from a split-and-duplex combination is not an unconditional permission on every parcel; an ADU is also not interchangeable with every primary unit. The profile keeps the general conditional reform and omits detailed current entitlement advice. The full statutory amendments and later case law were not audited; only the specified fact-sheet sections were reviewed.

sources.title: 13 March 2019 update: execution moratorium, continuing sentences and political objections
sources.findings: Read CalMatters’s report, including its explicit 13 March 2019 update. The page’s original 12 March publication and 2020 modification are not the execution-order date. It describes a moratorium on executions, continuing imprisonment and death sentences, and political objections from supporters of capital punishment. The action was not repeal of the death penalty, a pardon or automatic commutation/release. The then-current 737-prisoner count is not a 2026 count and is omitted. The original order, every individual case and later statewide death-penalty developments were not comprehensively reviewed.

sources.title: 16 November 2026: report of 15 November Lviv visit and medical-aid announcement
sources.findings: Read the governor’s 16 November 2026 Lviv release. It records an actual Sunday 15 November visit, meetings with regional officials, a cemetery visit and rehabilitation-related activities, and announces surplus medical equipment and supplies through a humanitarian partner. Publication on Monday is distinct from the Sunday visit; the dossier records 16 November public reporting of the aid arrangements. Announced donations are not proof that every bed, generator or bandage had arrived. Earlier 2022 shipments are separate from the new package. No claim of speaking for the federal government or independently inspecting delivery records is made.

sources.title: 16 November 2026: Lviv visit, surplus medical supplies and consideration of a 2028 presidential bid
sources.findings: Read the relevant body of AP’s 16 November 2026 report. It corroborates the Sunday Lviv visit and Monday announcement and describes a possible 2028 presidential run as under consideration. It does not establish a formal presidential candidacy or that his governorship had already ended. Delivery quantities and geopolitical claims outside the biographical scope are not adopted as independently verified outcomes. The source serves as independent corroboration of recent travel, not an audit of every statement in the governor’s announcement.

sources.title: 17 November 2026: completed congressional meetings seeking pending LA wildfire recovery funding
sources.findings: Read the 17 November 2026 official report of completed Washington meetings with lawmakers of both parties. The purpose was a supplemental recovery request for the January 2025 Los Angeles fires that remained unapproved by Congress. This is not evidence that funds were appropriated or received, nor that no other aid had ever been provided. The caption describes Jeffries as a future speaker, while the body correctly identifies his current minority-leader role; do not install him in a future office. Exact claimed permit, insurance and recovery figures and the attached letters were not independently reviewed. The completed meetings are the latest personal-activity evidence used here.

portraitReview.credit: Office of the Lieutenant Governor of California; uploaded by Tktru
portraitReview.unresolved: Read Commons description, California-government public-records rationale and full upload history. The record describes a lieutenant-governor portrait dated 10 January 2011, not a new 2019 or 2026 gubernatorial portrait. Tktru first uploaded a 320×353 version on 17 January 2011, a 480×720 version on 5 February 2011 and the current 1365×2048 higher-resolution version on 3 October 2012. The current page lists 462 KB, while the old evidence cache records different byte metadata; neither cached bytes nor current pixels are available for comparison. The credit belongs to the lieutenant governor’s office, not the uploader. Commons uses a state-government-work rationale with exceptions, not the U.S. federal-work rule or a CC BY licence. Its linked current ltg.ca.gov homepage now concerns Eleni Kounalakis and does not itself reproduce the historical source chain. Original image request on 18 November returned curl 22, HTTP 403 and reported HTTP 000; referenced cached JPEG is absent. Historical source correspondence, exact capture date beyond metadata, identity, colour and resolution require further verification before publication.
